title: Islam: one God
hookLine: the declaration of faith: there is no god but God, and Muhammad is God's messenger (Quran 112)

lines: A NEWBORN, A WHISPER IN THE EAR.
cards: A baby is born in a hospital in Cairo, or Jakarta, or Birmingham, Alabama. Within minutes, in many Muslim families, a father or grandfather leans close to the newborn's ear and softly speaks the call to prayer.
So among the first words that baby ever hears is a sentence about God. And at the other end of life, families gathered at a bedside hope the same sentence will be among the last words spoken.
First breath to last, one sentence frames it all: the shahada.

teach.b: Shahada means witness, or testimony. It's the declaration at the heart of Islam, naming God and the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him: la ilaha illa Allah, Muhammad rasul Allah.

There is no god but God, and Muhammad is the messenger of God. Allah is simply the Arabic word for God; Arab Christians use it too. The first half is about God: that God is one, with no partner and no rival.
Muslims call this oneness tawhid, and it's the center of everything else.
The second half is about the Prophet: that he is God's messenger, bringing the Qur'an. Saying the shahada sincerely, with understanding, is how a person becomes Muslim.
It's the first of the five pillars of Islam, repeated in every call to prayer, five times a day, from minarets around the world.
The Qur'an puts God's oneness most memorably in one of its shortest chapters, surah one hundred twelve.

teach.h: SAY: HE IS ALLAH, THE ONE.
teach.b: In Marmaduke Pickthall's 1930 translation: "Say: He is Allah, the One! Allah, the eternally Besought of all! He begetteth not nor was begotten. And there is none comparable unto Him." Four short lines.

In Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet is reported to have said this little chapter equals a third of the Qur'an, and many Muslims recite it every day. Notice the shape: first a negation, no god, then an affirmation, but God.
Many Muslim teachers say the negation clears the ground, all the false centers a life can have, money, status, fear, and the affirmation leaves only one.

how: Muslims say the shahada in every daily prayer and hear it in every call to prayer; many whisper the call to prayer to a newborn and hope to say the shahada as their last words.

o: a prayer said only on the day you convert
the witness that there is no god but God
a pledge of loyalty to a Muslim ruler

p: equal to a third of the Qur'an

s: Allah is a name only Muslims use for God
it's the Arabic word for God; Arab Christians use it too.
the shahada is the first of the five pillars
the testimony comes first; prayer, charity, fasting and pilgrimage follow.

from minarets, five times a day.

games.q: the shahada begins with a negation: there is no god. why start there?
o: to clear the ground, so only God is left: but God.
games.why: many Muslim teachers read it this way: the no clears away false centers, and the but God leaves only one.

practice: Breathe in, and let the mind be as busy as it is; breathe out, and quietly say, one. Each time a thought pulls at you, a worry, a plan, a craving, notice it, and come back: one.
If you're Muslim, you might hold the shahada itself; if not, let one be the only word in the room.

wordCard.voice: Shahada. Witness: there is no god but God, and Muhammad is the messenger of God. The first pillar of Islam. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: witness, testimony, the declaration of faith.

carryVoice: Your line: one. One God, with no partner and no rival, at the center. See you tomorrow.
